entries.title: Writing matters: leading writing instruction with a whole-school framework
entries.by: AERO
entries.summary: An AERO researcher and two classroom teachers walk through the School Writing Instruction Framework and what leading writing across a school involves.
staff: Which parts of the framework are already strong at our school, and which are missing?
What would a shared approach to sentence-level writing look like across our year levels?

entries.title: Harnessing the Science of Learning: book study recordings
entries.by: ONlit, with Nathaniel Swain and guests
entries.summary: A six-part book study on Nathaniel Swain's Harnessing the Science of Learning, with guest experts joining each session.
staff: Which idea from this session challenges something we currently do?
What is one small change we could each trial before the next session?

entries.by: Evidence Based Education
entries.summary: Five short animations on memory, dual coding, retrieval practice, deliberate practice, and spacing and interleaving. Easy to drop into a staff meeting.
staff: Where does this idea already show up in our lessons?
What would it look like to use it more deliberately next week?

entries.title: Leading explicit teaching: information session
entries.by: NSW Department of Education
entries.summary: Jarrad Cox from the department's curriculum team walks leaders through the explicit teaching workshops, strategy modules and technique guides, and the thinking behind how to roll them out.
staff: Which of these workshops or strategy modules would best suit where our staff are now?
What shared understanding of how learning happens do we need before we work on individual strategies?

entries.title: AI and Assessment: What Needs to Change
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Daisy Christodoulou
entries.summary: Daisy Christodoulou reviews what research shows about AI marking and feedback on student writing, drawing on No More Marking trials, and what assessment may need to change.

entries.title: The Differentiation Conundrum: How to Pair Explicit Instruction with High Potential Learning
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Kate Barton
entries.summary: Dr Kate Barton weighs the evidence on differentiation and ability grouping, then shows ways to add depth and stretch for high potential students within explicit teaching, with K-12 examples.

entries.title: Building on a Strong Foundation in Phonics, Part 1
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Mandy Nayton
entries.summary: Mandy Nayton gives a short history of English, explains lexical quality and outlines teaching that builds spelling and vocabulary in middle and upper primary. Part 1 of two.

entries.title: Tier 1 Instruction is Risk Reduction
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Stephanie Stollar
entries.summary: Stephanie Stollar tackles three common misunderstandings about Tier 1 reading instruction and shows how screening, diagnostic and progress data can shape core teaching that reduces risk.

entries.title: MTSS in Specialist Schools: Same-Same or Different?
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Charlotte Peverett
entries.summary: Charlotte Peverett explains what Tier 1, 2 and 3 look like in specialist settings and which practices give the most benefit for students in those schools.

entries.title: Evidence Informed Teaching
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Peps Mccrea
entries.summary: Peps Mccrea sets out a framework of five evidence-informed strategies teachers can use to lift learning, motivation and equity.

entries.title: Introduction to MTSS in Practice: Building Strong Tier 1 Instruction and Aligned Tier 2 Support
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Stephanie Dehghani, Templestowe Heights Primary School
entries.summary: Assistant principal Stephanie Dehghani describes how Templestowe Heights Primary built strong Tier 1 teaching, aligned Tier 2 as an extra dose of core instruction and used data to decide support.
staff: Is our Tier 2 an extra dose of what we teach in class, or a separate program?

entries.title: From Framework to Practice: Getting Tier 1 Right and Tier 2 Working
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Kylie Hoey
entries.summary: Kylie Hoey works through the practical problems of MTSS in a primary school, from protecting Tier 1, timetabling and staffing to what to do when too many students need extra support.

entries.title: Epic Fluency Instruction: Strategy Instruction and Practice (Session 1)
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Kat O'Rourke
entries.summary: NSW teacher Kat O'Rourke shows how she sequences strategy instruction and practice to build number fact fluency in a 15-minute daily block, and what she learned implementing it.

entries.title: Vocabulary: Lyn Stone's 4-Step Process in the Study of Words
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Lyn Stone
entries.summary: Lyn Stone demonstrates her four-step process for studying a word in depth, bringing together phonics, morphology, spelling, syntax and etymology.

entries.title: Minds versus Machines: A Very Short History
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Benjamin Riley
entries.summary: Benjamin Riley tells the story of how cognitive science emerged from the mid-century contest between behaviourism and mentalism, and argues it still matters for teaching today.

entries.title: The Maths Guarantee: How to Implement Great Primary Maths Teaching
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Amy Haywood and Nick Parkinson, Grattan Institute
entries.summary: Grattan Institute's Amy Haywood and Nick Parkinson summarise the evidence on primary maths teaching and share lessons from seven case study schools that put it into practice.

entries.title: Improving Maths Outcomes with Universal Screening
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Brad Nguyen, Docklands Primary School
entries.summary: Brad Nguyen explains how Docklands Primary uses the Acadience Math universal screener, what the assessment involves and how the results inform support and school improvement.

entries.title: Building Strong Writers in Lower Primary: Structured, Explicit Instruction from Sentence to Text Level
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Polly Anderson, Serpentine Primary School
entries.summary: Polly Anderson shares the routines Serpentine Primary uses to move early writers from oral sentences to short narratives and reports, including how scaffolds are faded.
staff: How much oral rehearsal do our youngest students get before they write?
Which of these routines could we trial in Foundation to Year 2 this term?

entries.title: What Do We Mean by a Knowledge-rich Curriculum?
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Heather Fearn
entries.summary: Heather Fearn of Ark returns to first principles on why knowledge matters, what a knowledge-rich curriculum means for lesson design and the common pitfalls when schools adopt one.

entries.title: Responsive Teaching with Carl Hendrick
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Carl Hendrick
entries.summary: Carl Hendrick looks at how teachers can use in-the-moment evidence of student understanding to adapt instruction. The second of his two sessions for Think Forward Educators.

entries.title: Checking for Understanding: A Powerful Lever of Learning Every Teacher Should Know
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Carl Hendrick
entries.summary: Carl Hendrick explains how to tell real understanding from recognition, covering retrieval practice, diagnostic questions and using misconceptions to make student thinking visible.

Which misconception in an upcoming unit could we write a diagnostic question for?

entries.title: Building Background Knowledge
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Jillian Robinson
entries.summary: Jillian Robinson introduces four Teach Like a Champion tools for building background knowledge to support comprehension, including embedded non-fiction and knowledge organisers, with classroom footage.

entries.title: Structuring Explicit Maths Lessons
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Samantha Charlton, Templestowe Heights Primary School
entries.summary: Samantha Charlton unpacks the parts of an explicit maths lesson aligned with the VTLM 2.0, covering review, teaching new content, guided and independent practice, fluency and in-lesson assessment.

How do we decide when students are ready to move from guided to independent practice?

entries.title: An Introduction to Bar Modelling
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Jess Easton
entries.summary: Jess Easton shows how bar models bridge concrete materials and abstract calculation, and how to pair them with written methods so students see the structure of a problem.

entries.title: Explicit Teaching and Problem Solving, Using the Instructional Hierarchy
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Sean Alston
entries.summary: Sean Alston explains the four stages of the Instructional Hierarchy and uses primary maths examples to show when to teach explicitly and when problem solving fits.

entries.title: Teaching Maths Using the Victorian Lesson Plans
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Sacha Giurietto
entries.summary: Sacha Giurietto walks through the Victorian Department of Education's free maths lesson plans, the position statement behind them and how schools can use them to teach maths explicitly.

entries.title: Key Instructional Routines in the Primary Mathematics Classroom
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Ollie Lovell, Toni Hatten-Roberts and David Morkunas
entries.summary: Ollie Lovell, Toni Hatten-Roberts and David Morkunas take teachers through the core instructional routines that keep every student thinking in primary maths, whatever program a school uses.

entries.title: Teaching Maths Explicitly in Small Schools
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Jane St John, Jonathan Nettelbeck and Michelle Lastrilla
entries.summary: Staff from three small and regional schools describe how they organise multi-age classes, lessons, planning and intervention to teach maths explicitly, and the challenges they still face.

entries.title: The Benefits of Fact Fluency when Teaching Mathematics
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Brian Poncy
entries.summary: Dr Brian Poncy reviews research on five ways fluent recall of basic facts supports later maths learning, and shares results from a five-year study.

entries.title: Developing a Knowledge-Rich Subject Curriculum
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Heather Fearn
entries.summary: Heather Fearn's follow-up session on how specialists and non-specialists can build and quality assure a subject curriculum, and why hierarchical and cumulative subjects need different sequencing.

entries.title: Leading Assessment
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Sacha Giurietto and Reid Smith
entries.summary: Sacha Giurietto and Reid Smith explain how to set up a whole-school assessment system and run data meetings that lead to changes in teaching.

Which assessments do we collect but rarely act on?

entries.title: Phonics Plus in the Classroom: Practical Strategies for Success

entries.title: Why Maths Lessons Fail and How to Make Success Inevitable
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Brendan Lee

entries.title: 1% Better Every Day: Practical Advice for the Evidence-Informed Teacher
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Stuart Kime
entries.summary: Stuart Kime considers what research says about how teachers build expertise through knowledge, skills and habits, and offers techniques to try in your own practice.

entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with David Didau
entries.summary: David Didau explains how speech and writing differ and shows structured talk routines that lighten cognitive load and give students practice with academic English before they write.

entries.title: Implementing MTSS in Secondary Schools: Challenges and Strategies
entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Jessica Colleu Terradas

entries.summary: Teachers bring real problems they have met putting the science of learning into practice, and Nathaniel Swain and Brendan Lee coach them towards evidence-informed solutions.

entries.by: Think Forward Educators, with Sarah Kelly

entries.title: Engaged Classrooms Through Effective Classroom Management

entries.summary: Amy Haywood presents Grattan Institute findings on the planning load teachers carry alone, and how five schools set up shared whole-school curriculum planning.

entries.by: Branching Minds, with Amanda VanDerHeyden
entries.summary: Amanda VanDerHeyden's keynote on lessons learned from 15 years of multi-tiered systems of support, hosted by Branching Minds. Useful for leaders reviewing their own MTSS.

entries.title: Morphology and spelling, with Lyn Stone
entries.by: The Reading League Illinois, with Lyn Stone
entries.summary: Lyn Stone presents on morphology and spelling for The Reading League Illinois. A long session for teachers wanting to deepen their knowledge of how words are built.

entries.title: Learning through and to talk: why oracy matters, with Voice 21
entries.by: Education Scotland, with Voice 21
entries.summary: Voice 21 presents on why oracy matters, learning both through talk and to talk, in a session hosted by Education Scotland. Useful for teachers planning how talk is taught.

entries.title: Science of Reading Presentation by Pamela Snow
entries.by: Catholic Education Canberra Goulburn, with Pamela Snow
entries.summary: Professor Pamela Snow presents on the science of reading, in a session recorded for Catholic Education Canberra Goulburn's Catalyst program.

entries.title: Reading instruction in Australian schools: Headwinds, tailwinds and crosswinds
entries.by: Mornington Peninsula Foundation, with Pamela Snow
entries.summary: Pamela Snow's 2025 La Trobe Oration asks why reading instruction is still contested after decades of research, what has slowed research reaching classrooms, and what needs to change in teacher education.

entries.title: Oral language development and reading, with Professor Pamela Snow
entries.by: Spellcaster Education, with Pamela Snow
entries.summary: Professor Pamela Snow speaks about oral language development and its relationship to reading, in a session hosted by Spellcaster Education.

entries.title: Stephanie Le Lievre: A knowledge-based comprehension model
entries.by: Read Ballarat, with Stephanie Le Lievre
entries.summary: Stephanie Le Lievre presents a knowledge-based model of reading comprehension in a session for Read Ballarat. Useful for teachers rethinking how comprehension is taught.
